claim: An incompatible SAME-DIMENSION embedding model change is rejected at MCP boot, because dimension agreement is not compatibility.

implemented.module: mcp/servers/lib/embedding-identity.js — probes a frozen text and fingerprints the 4-decimal-quantised vector (sha256-16). The fingerprint is a property of the deployed model and its preprocessing, not of the EMBEDDING_MODEL name.
implemented.enforcement: mcp/servers/ruvector-mcp.cjs boot: a fingerprint mismatch against the pin is FATAL (process.exit(1)). Unpinned or unprobeable is advisory — a known-bad identity is refused; a pin is never invented.
implemented.supervised_override: RUVECTOR_EMBED_IDENTITY_OVERRIDE must name the exact divergent fingerprint. There is no boolean that means 'trust me'.

measured.stability: Probed three times across two processes; identical every time, which is what makes it usable as a gate rather than a source of false alarms.

remaining: The pin was frozen from the currently deployed model rather than from an independent statement of what SHOULD be deployed.
A model swap still needs a corpus re-embed and a passing recall receipt before the pin is moved; that sequence is documented, not automated.
Preprocessing beyond the 2,000-character embed prefix (tokeniser, pooling) is captured only indirectly, through its effect on the fingerprint.
